mutants.note: No test gave an 11-character date with dashes in place. terms.test.mjs now asserts 2026-07-011 is refused. Line since replaced by the shared period.mjs parser.

(Y!=y && M!=m) || D!=d vs Y!=y || M!=m || D!=d: they differ only when the day matches and exactly one of year/month differs. A matching day means the day was in range, so the only rollover is an out-of-range month (00, 13-99), which always changes both year and month index. A day rollover always changes the day (it drops by at least 28). No input separates them; the line was then replaced by the shared period.mjs parser.

real_defects.issue: parseIsoDate (copied in terms.mjs and checks.mjs isoDate) checked only length and dash positions, then Number(): '2026-+7-01', '2026-07- 1', '-001-01-01', '+202-01-01' parsed as real dates, so an invoice with such an issue date passed INV-003 (also INV-020 due date, INV-042 period, terms) in the web and server checker while the Python mirror (date.fromisoformat) rejected them. Date.UTC also mapped years 0-99 to 1900s, so the JS refused valid '0050-01-01'. Fixed: one strict [0-9] parser with setUTCFullYear in period.mjs, imported by checks.mjs and terms.mjs; date-parity.test.mjs compares JS vs the three Python parsers on 3031 strings (141 disagreements on the old code, 0 after).

certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
